Every decision is labelled by what the player can responsibly know.
This demo keeps the Aurora scenario fictional and does not hide an unbundled NASA data claim.

SIMULATED  ·  Aurora Station / 2046 mission
Fictional station, cadets, dates and game resources. Used for the training scenario.

TRAINING SCENARIO  ·  36-hour night and Earth-link cutoff
The night is sized to a published Shackleton-rim site (Mazarico et al. 2011). In the computed April 2046 sky (JPL Horizons), Earth is below the exact pole's horizon and rising all night, so the shift-4 Earth-link cutoff is an authored training event.

OBSERVED + COMPUTED  ·  Chapter 1 sources (each Data Card shows its dataset ID and link)
NASA JPL Horizons (Sun and Earth positions) · NASA DONKI and NOAA GOES-13 (the 10 Sep 2017 storm) · LRO LOLA illumination study, Mazarico et al. 2011 · NASA BVAD 2022 (air and food) · NASA 10 kW solar array study · Townsend et al. 1988 and Clowdsley 2021, NASA Langley (water shielding) · NASA OSDR and Wisconsin Fast Plants (Brassica rapa).

DOCUMENTED  ·  NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
Made by an independent team for the challenge. No NASA endorsement is implied.

AI disclosure: AI tools made this game's 3D models and animation, cutscene images and video, and all voices, music and sound effects, and wrote the game code to the team's specifications. The story, dialogue, puzzle rules, numbers and science mapping are the team's. Every generation is logged in production/AI_PROMPT_LOG.md (summary: docs/AI_USE.md).
Accessibility: captions, readable text, pause-safe decisions and timer-free progression are the default route.
